turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on at, on and in for time?
turns.tutor:
Rule: at with clock times, on with days and dates, in with months and years.
Right: "The film starts at six o'clock."
Wrong: "The film starts in six o'clock." Six o'clock is a clock time, not a month.
I show you one: "The zoo is closed on Saturday." Saturday is a day. So: on.
Your turn. Write in, on or at:
My train leaves ___ 5 o'clock.
